summary: Every published NUMBER re-derives exactly from the raw JSONL, and every substantive runtime CONCLUSION survived adversarial probing — including two that I had to run new controls to settle, both of which came back in the author's favour. What does not survive is the evidence bookkeeping: the central v1.19.3 claim ('a delegate declaring no effort: inherits the session's level') held the session level CONSTANT at xhigh across all 20 delegate runs, so as published it could not distinguish inheritance from a fixed xhigh default — I ran the missing arm and it confirms inheritance, but the file shipped the conclusion without the discriminating control, which is the exact error its own Method warning names. And v1.19.4's headline — 'the spawn rule is now verified on the path it prescribes' — is false as written: it re-verified 2 of the matrix's 7 rows on the frontmatter path; the matrix column is still labelled 'agent frontmatter' while 5 rows were measured through --agents JSON. 2 refuted claims, 10 requiring correction, 0 wrong runtime conclusions.

reproduction.method: Re-derived every count directly from *.jsonl: WebSearch call control via grep -c '"name":"WebSearch"'; failure signal via grep -c 'output_config.effort'; tier actually rejected via grep -o "output_config.effort '[a-z]*'"; model actually run via the type=system/subtype=init .model field (NOT the raw grep, which also matches assistant-message model fields); delegate identity via '"subagent_type":"..."'; verbatim outcome via jq 'select(.type=="result")|.result'.
reproduction.session_matrix: REPRODUCES EXACTLY. ctlhigh 2 runs: 0 x 400, RESULTS=7. base 3/3 fail, 1m 3/3 + pilot1m 1/1 = 4/4 fail, flagxhigh 3/3 fail, ultra 2/2 fail. 12 failing runs total, 2 rejections each = 24; tally 'xhigh' x20 + 'max' x4 — matches the published counts to the unit. WebSearch call control WS>=1 present in all 22 session runs.
reproduction.model_matrix: REPRODUCES EXACTLY. son-xh, son-max, fab-xh, fab-max = 8 runs, 0 x 400, RESULTS=7 in all 8, init model claude-sonnet-5 / claude-fable-5 as claimed.
reproduction.delegate_matrix: REPRODUCES EXACTLY, all 7 rows, 16 runs. inherit 3/3 ok, sonnet 2 + pilot 1 = 3/3 ok (ag-pilot-1 confirmed subagent_type=sonnet-searcher, so folding it into the 3 is legitimate), plain 2/2 fail@xhigh, xh 2/2 fail@xhigh, narrow 2/2 NOTOOL with WS=0, envhigh 2/2 fail@xhigh, envsonnet 2/2 ok. Delegate-model control confirmed: only claude-opus-5 appears in inherit/plain/xh streams; claude-sonnet-5 appears in the model-pinned rows.
reproduction.frontmatter_matrix: REPRODUCES EXACTLY. fm-high 2/2 ok (0 x 400, RESULTS=7), fm-plain 2/2 fail quoting 'xhigh'; both arms ran on claude-opus-5 only.
reproduction.no_missing_or_mislabelled_runs: The 'ultra' label is NOT ultracode despite the name — it is --effort max (CLAUDE_EFFORT=max, 400 quotes 'max', settings pins xhigh so only the flag can produce max; devlog #0025's own table lists it as --effort max and carries no ultracode row). Attribution in the shipped table is correct.

claims.location: native-capabilities.md, Effort § bug bullet — session matrix
claims.claim: The trigger is the tier, not how the tier was set: high searches, xhigh and max do not; neither mechanism nor model variant moves the outcome.
claims.checked: 12/12 failures re-derived; each failing run states its own tier in the 400, so no row rests on an assumed level; discrimination control present (ctlhigh returns RESULTS=7, so the rig can show success); precedence control present (--effort high beat settings' effortLevel:xhigh, proving the flag mechanism is live); WebSearch-was-called control present in all 22 runs.
claims.notes: This is the strongest part of the release. The oracle is genuinely independent of the claim — the API names the tier it rejected.

claims.location: native-capabilities.md 'A delegate that declares no effort: inherits the session's level'; harness-discipline.md same; CHANGELOG 1.19.3 bullet 3
claims.claim: A delegate declaring no effort: inherits the session's level (replacing the earlier 'stays at the model default').
claims.checked: THE SESSION LEVEL WAS xhigh IN ALL 20 DELEGATE RUNS — 16 via --agents, 4 via frontmatter. A variable held constant across every row cannot be the one the matrix attributes the outcome to. As published, 'plain delegate 400s quoting xhigh' is exactly as consistent with 'the ad-hoc delegate default is xhigh' as with inheritance; the 400 tells you the delegate's level, not where that level came from. Note the direction of the error: the claim it REPLACED ('stays at the model default') did vary the parent session (low vs xhigh) and merely had a weak oracle. v1.19.3 swapped a varied-but-weak measurement for a strong-but-unvaried one and inverted the conclusion. This is the same class of defect as v1.19.0 ('a matrix that never varies the variable proves nothing, confidently') and v1.19.1, in a third form.
claims.resolution: I ran the missing arm (CTL-1): session --effort high + plain-searcher -> 2/2 RESULTS=7, zero rejections, delegate on claude-opus-5. That refutes the fixed-default alternative and confirms inheritance. The conclusion is correct; it was shipped without the control that establishes it.
claims.correction: Add the varied-session control to the bullet, e.g.: 'from an xhigh session a delegate declaring nothing fails 2/2 quoting xhigh; from a `high` session the same delegate searches 2/2 — the delegate's level tracks the session's.' Cite ctl-plainhigh-*.jsonl. Without it the file asserts a causal direction its matrix structurally cannot show.

claims.location: .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md step B3.5 (dev-harness commit 3ff5002): 'Зелёный — приложи артефакт в .claude/audits/'
claims.claim: (process) The refuter artifact is retained as part of the repo's evidence trail.
